architecture.type: four-level hierarchical residual CNN with global context gate
architecture.input_receptive_field_pixels: whole image via global context gate

affine_field.application: source + .25*(full-resolution detail + learned 3x4 affine color correction)

limitations: One scene and first-reset frames only; a spatial or camera holdout is not cross-scene generalization.
No temporal training or quality validation.

output_grading.scope: Unfitted algebraic approximation from the same runtime controls; other camera views reuse the parameters by inference.
output_grading.training: Differentiable FP32 operations after the clamped learned residual.
output_grading.inference: FP16 network, FP32 grading, FP16 final storage; all included in graph timing.

rejected_without_explicit_interpolation_.scope: Finite FP16 affine/detail composition only; not a native renderer benchmark or model quality test.

corrected_seventeen_case_check.scope: Finite FP16 affine/detail composition only; not a native renderer benchmark or model quality test.

tests.label: input undershoot overshoot and output clipping

accepted_eighteen_case_check.scope: Finite FP16 affine/detail composition only; not a native renderer benchmark or model quality test.

composition_kernel.scope: Finite FP16 operation parity with Torch, not exhaustive arithmetic or native NVIDIA output parity.

post_training_branch_ablation.scope: Post-training branch ablation only; no retraining or latency claim.

findings: The prior student has about 79.6% and 82.5% of validation squared error at spatial wavelengths of at least 64 pixels.
Adding the affine field slightly worsens both validation MAEs; the new model is rejected.
The affine branch explains much of the original training-view color change but transfers weakly to the validation cameras.
Fusing composition and the existing output grade reduces this complete student graph from 3.683 ms to 1.199 ms with identical tested output.
The isolated composition takes 0.0655 ms versus 1.248 ms in Torch. This does not accelerate the native NVIDIA renderer.
limitations: Eighteen training images and two repeatedly consulted validation cameras from one scene; not an independent final test set.
First-reset frames only; no cross-scene, temporal, UI or perceptual quality acceptance.
CUDA Graph times exclude D3D12 integration. No student was installed in the application benchmark or WuWa.
Historical timing differences between architectures do not establish an architectural speedup.
Disabled branches in ablations are still computed and then discarded; no retraining or branch speedup is claimed.
The interpolated color field is not a complete HDRNet implementation and cannot alone represent all neural detail.
Only source, hashes and numeric evidence are published; images, weights and vendor code remain private.
